Agreement No. CE 4/2024 (HY)
Northern Metropolis Highway
– Investigation
Environmental Impact Assessment Report – San Tin Section
INTRODUCTION
Project Title
1.1.1.1 The title of the Project is “Northern Metropolis Highway – San Tin Section”
(hereafter referred to as the Project).
1.1.1.2 The Project is one of the four sections of the Northern Metropolis Highway (NMH),
with the other three being the Tin Shui Wai Section, Kwu Tung Section and New
Territories North (NTN) New Town Section. The NMH has an overall length of
approximately 24 km.
Project Background
1.2.1.1 In December 2020, the Transport Department (TD) commissioned a consultancy
study titled “Strategic Study on Major Roads beyond 2030 – Feasibility Study”
(SSMR FS) under Agreement No. CE 7/2018 (TT). The SSMR FS examined the
future configuration of Hong Kong’s major road infrastructure to ensure that the
planning of major transport infrastructure will drive or even reserve capacity to meet
Hong Kong's long-term development needs, including those proposed in the
Northern Metropolis Development Strategy.
1.2.1.2 The 2022 Policy Address mentioned that three major road projects recommended
under the Strategy Study on Major Roads beyond 2030 (SSMR2030+) would be
taken forward to create a highly interconnected and accessible road network,
significantly driving and supporting Hong Kong's future development. NMH is one
of the three major road projects.
1.2.1.3 The 2023 Policy Address announced an extension of the NMH proposal to the east,
connecting it to the Sha Tau Kok Road Interchange.
1.2.1.4 The NMH aims to establish a new strategic route improving east-west connectivity
within the Northern Metropolis and reduce potential traffic congestion on Yuen Long
Highway, San Tin Highway, and Fanling Highway.
1.2.1.5 The NMH is being taken forward following the principle of “Holistic Planning and
Phased Implementation”. The investigation study for the entire NMH will be
completed first, followed by detailed design and construction of individual sections
to cater for the development needs and suit the allocation of public resources. The
San Tin Section is tentatively ready for tendering in Year 2027. Subject to the further
planning and the actual implementation of the Project, advance works and the
associated study would tentatively commence in the same year or Year 2028 with
target commissioning of the Project in or before 2036.
1.2.1.6 The NMH will take into account the transport infrastructure projects in the pipeline,
including the capacity of roads and railways, overall cost-effectiveness and
allocation of public resources, etc., in formulating a more concrete implementation
programme, with a view to completing the remaining sections of the NMH in phases
in about 3 to 4 years after the commissioning of the San Tin Section.
1.2.1.7 Being a part of the Northern Metropolis Highway, the Project comprises mainly a
dual three-lane carriageway in the form of at-grade road, tunnel and viaduct, starts
from the interchange of Yuen Long Highway / Tsing Long Highway on the west and

Agreement No. CE 4/2024 (HY)
Northern Metropolis Highway
– Investigation
Environmental Impact Assessment Report – San Tin Section
1.3.1.2 A Project Profile (PP) (No. PP-683/2025) for the Project based on the 8.5-kilometer-
long alignment in the earlier stage of the Study was submitted to the Environmental
Protection Department (EPD) on 22 April 2025 for the application for an EIA Study
Brief under Section 5(1)(a) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance
(EIAO). An EIA Study Brief No. ESB-373/2025 was subsequently issued on 5 June
2025.
1.3.1.3 Subsequent to the issue of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Study Brief
(No. ESB-373/2025), some changes were made to the project boundary, layout and
design to facilitate the project development. In accordance with Clause 6.2 of the
EIA Study Brief, confirmation had been sought from the Director of Environmental
Protection in writing to confirm that the scope of issues covered by the EIA Study
Brief (No. ESB-373/2025) can still cover the key changes, and the additional issues,
if any, that the EIA report must address. Having reviewed the proposed changes,
EPD confirmed that the EIA Study Brief is still valid.
Purpose of the EIA Study
1.4.1.1 The purpose of this EIA study as stated in the EIA Study Brief (No. ESB-373/2025)
is to provide information on the nature and extent of environmental impacts arising
from the construction and operation stages of the Project and associated activities
that will take place concurrently. This information will contribute to decisions by the
Director of Environmental Protection on:
(i) the overall acceptability of any adverse environmental consequences that are
likely to arise as a result of the Project;
(ii) the conditions and requirements for the detailed design, construction and
operation of the Project to mitigate against adverse environmental
consequences wherever practicable; and
(iii) the acceptability of residual impacts after the proposed mitigation measures
are implemented.
Objective of the EIA Study
1.5.1.1 The objectives of the EIA study as stated in the EIA Study Brief (No. ESB-373/2025)
are as follows:
(i) to describe the Project and associated works together with the requirements
and environmental benefits for carrying out the Project;
(ii) to identify and describe the elements of the community and environment likely
to be affected by the Project and/or likely to cause adverse impacts to the
Project, including both the natural and man-made environment and the
associated environmental constraints;
(iii) to identify and quantify emission sources and determine the significance of
impacts on sensitive receivers and potential affected uses, and to propose
measures to mitigate these impacts;
